title: 1990 AHSME Problem 26
statement: Ten people form a circle. Each picks a number and tells it to the two neighbors adjacent to him in the circle. Then each person computes and announces the average of the numbers of his two neighbors. The figure shows the average announced by each person (not the original number the person picked). The number picked by the person who announced the average \(6\) was

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: not uniquely determined from the given information

solutions.text:
Index the displayed averages \(a_0,a_1,\ldots,a_9\) clockwise as \(1,2,\ldots,10,\) and let \(x_i\) be the corresponding picked numbers. Write \(x_0=t,\ x_1=u.\) From \(x_{i-1}+x_{i+1}=2a_i,\) successive values are \[ \begin{aligned} x_2&=4-t, &x_3&=6-u,\\ x_4&=4+t, &x_5&=4+u,\\ x_6&=8-t, &x_7&=10-u,\\ x_8&=8+t, &x_9&=8+u. \end{aligned} \] The two closing equations give \(t=6\) and \(u=-3.\) Hence \(x_5=4+u=1.\)

Thus the correct answer is A.
hints: If \(x_i\) is a picked number and \(a_i\) the displayed average, then \(x_{i-1}+x_{i+1}=2a_i\)
Start with two unknown adjacent picked numbers and propagate around the circle
